payload.objective: Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of STAT3-p.Arg382Trp (STAT3, UniProt P40763) and test it with one targeted computational test.
payload.question: For a pathogenic missense variant in an immune-deficiency gene, which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function, and does a targeted computational test change the conclusion that the starting evidence suggested?

payload.statement: ClinVar classifies NM_139276.3(STAT3):c.1144C>T (p.Arg382Trp) as Pathogenic for Hyper-IgE recurrent infection syndrome 1, autosomal dominant, with the disease note "STAT3 gain of function"; criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts.
payload.strength: criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts (2 of 4 stars)

payload.statement: UniProtKB natural variant VAR_037367 at residue 382 (R to W) is annotated as Hyper-IgE recurrent infection syndrome 1, loss of function, with reduced DNA-binding ability; 5 publications cited.
AlphaMissense gives p.Arg382Trp of P40763 a pathogenicity score of 0.9966, classed as likely pathogenic.
ScoreCons conservation at P40763 residue 382 is 0.974 (0 to 1 scale, higher more conserved across species).
EVE classes p.Arg382Trp of P40763 as pathogenic with a score of 0.804 (0 to 1 scale); popEVE is -5.334 (more negative is more deleterious).
Four experimental X-ray structures (6NJS, 6QHD, 6TLC, 6NUQ) observe residue 382 of P40763 and all four carry the reference arginine; none carries the mutation.
payload.strength: X-ray diffraction, 2.7 to 3.15 Å; PDBe SIFTS residue mapping

payload.statement: Ligand KQV (compound SD36 and SI109 series) is bound in the STAT3 core in PDB 6NJS and 6NUQ; the ligand list covers all four observing structures and contains only this one non-solvent ligand.
UniProtKB annotates STAT3 as a homodimer or heterodimer with STAT1, and the SH2 domain spans residues 580-670, outside the DNA-binding domain that contains residue 382.
InterPro places residue 382 within the STAT transcription factor DNA-binding domain (residues 326-464).
ClinVar lists R382Q, R382L and R382P as also Pathogenic at the same residue, so several substitutions at residue 382 are recorded as pathogenic.
A 2025 Science Advances study reports STAT3 haploinsufficiency as associated with autosomal dominant hyper-IgE syndrome, and states that most AD-HIES STAT3 variants are considered dominant negative.

A 2021 J Exp Med study tested 143 STAT3 variants and reports that only six of 135 reported in-frame variants had been experimentally shown to be dominant negative, so most AD-HIES variant mechanisms were not yet tested.
No retrieved record shows a direct DNA-binding or dominant-negative measurement for R382W; the UniProt loss-of-function label rests on cited studies whose content was not retrieved.
payload.why_it_matters: Without that measurement, DNA-binding loss and dominant-negative interference cannot be separated from the records alone.

payload.statement: The records do not say which residues contact DNA or which side chain atoms R382 makes with DNA or partner proteins.
payload.why_it_matters: A direct R382 DNA contact would favour the nucleic-acid mechanism over a folding defect.

payload.statement: ClinVar's disease note calls R382W a STAT3 gain of function, while UniProt annotates the same residue change as loss of function with reduced DNA binding.
payload.why_it_matters: The direction of the effect is in conflict across sources, so any mechanism must explain a loss-of-function readout for a variant filed as gain of function.

payload.statement: R382W removes an arginine side chain that contacts DNA in the STAT3 DNA-binding domain, so the mutant protein binds its target DNA poorly and the response is lost.
payload.would_refute: A structural test shows R382 has no contact with DNA or within-domain ligand-free pocket context, and the variant keeps DNA-binding in an assay.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: UniProt reports reduced DNA-binding for this exact substitution (E2) and the residue is highly conserved (E4) and predicted pathogenic by AlphaMissense (E3), placing it first.

payload.statement: R382W destabilises the DNA-binding domain fold, so the mutant domain is partly unfolded or misfolded and fails to bind DNA.
payload.would_refute: A predicted folding free-energy change near zero, with the variant residue solvent-exposed and not packed in the domain core.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The residue sits inside the DNA-binding domain and is highly conserved (E4, E5), which fits a folding defect, but no stability measurement is yet in the record.

payload.statement: R382W mutant STAT3 subunits pair with wild-type STAT3 in a dimer that is inactive, so the variant acts dominant-negatively by blocking the wild-type protein.
payload.would_refute: The variant behaves as haploinsufficient with no dominant effect on co-expressed wild-type STAT3, or the residue is far from the dimer interface.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: UniProt records STAT3 homodimer formation (E8), and the 2021 study says most AD-HIES variants act this way (E-OpenAlex), but no record places R382 at the dimer interface, so it ranks last.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change of R382W on the AlphaFold model. A destabilising value supports H2; a neutral value weakens H2 and leaves H1 and H3 open.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A destabilising value would move H2 up; a neutral value would move H2 down and make H1 (DNA contact loss) the leading explanation. Either outcome changes the ranking.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: list_available_tests reports the FoldX prediction state as ok and the test can run now with no approval and no compute seconds.
controls: Within-site comparison: the same predictor for the other substitutions reported at this residue.
Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.

payload.description: Predicted pocket and predicted protein-protein interface membership of R382 on the AlphaFold model. Interface membership would support H3; absence weakens H3.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A residue in a predicted interface would raise H3; ProtVar already reports interface state as None, so the likely outcome is a weakening of H3 with little change to H1 or H2.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: ProtVar pocket and interface data answer for this residue and P2Rank runs on the AlphaFold model; no approval needed and no compute seconds.
controls: Rank control: the rank and probability of the pocket among all predicted pockets of the model.
Confidence control: mean pLDDT of the pocket residues.

payload.description: Reference versus variant structure prediction of the 182-581 construct. Would test local rearrangement for H2 and H1.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: A confident local rearrangement would support H2, but structure predictors are not validated for single substitutions, so the effect on ranking is weaker than stability.
payload.feasibility_reasoning: can_run is false: ESM Atlas did not answer within 20 s and no cached output exists for this variant; the test also needs human approval and costs 120 compute seconds.
controls: Same provider, model version and construct for both sequences.
Residues with low confidence in either model are masked before the RMSD is computed.

payload.rationale: T1 (FoldX stability) directly separates the folding hypothesis H2 from the DNA-contact hypothesis H1, costs no compute seconds and needs no approval. T2 mainly bears on H3 and ProtVar already reports no interface, so it is expected to add less. T3 cannot run now and needs approval for 120 compute seconds.

rejected.reason: Interface membership bears mainly on H3; ProtVar already reports interface state None, so expected learning is lower than T1.
Cannot run now (ESM Atlas did not answer, no cached output) and needs human approval for 120 compute seconds, so feasibility is 0.1.

payload.findings: review_claims checked 22 statements: no clinical or treatment wording, no evidence without a source, no unlabelled hypotheses. Evidence items 12, hypotheses 3. Chosen test T1 (stability_effect) needs no approval: it reads public database records and starts no job, costs 0 compute seconds.

payload.summary: FoldX predicts a folding free-energy change of +1.96 kcal/mol for R382W on the AlphaFold model, below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold, at residue pLDDT 88.0. The same predictor gives R382L +0.80, R382P +1.79 and R382Q +2.23 kcal/mol at the same residue.

values.headline: FoldX predicts ΔΔG +1.96 kcal/mol for R382W, below the destabilising threshold of 2.0 kcal/mol (residue pLDDT 88.0).

Applicability control: the model confidence (pLDDT) at the residue, because FoldX on a low-confidence region is not interpretable.
limitations: FoldX on a predicted model is a computational prediction with errors near 1 kcal/mol.
A neutral stability prediction does not show the variant is tolerated.

per_hypothesis.why: Predicted stability change is not destabilising (+1.96 kcal/mol, E-T1 result), so the variant does not need a fold defect to explain loss of function; this leaves a direct DNA-contact loss as the simplest explanation, consistent with the UniProt reduced DNA-binding annotation [E2]. This is a relative shift, not a direct test of DNA binding.

The predicted change of +1.96 kcal/mol sits just under the 2.0 kcal/mol threshold at a confident residue (pLDDT 88.0), and R382Q, also a recorded pathogenic substitution at this residue [E10], is predicted more destabilising at +2.23 kcal/mol, so stability alone does not explain why R382W is loss of function.
The stability test does not measure dimer contact, so H3 is neither supported nor refuted by this result.

payload.uncertainty: FoldX on a predicted model has errors near 1 kcal/mol, and the value sits 0.04 kcal/mol below the threshold, so the neutral call is marginal. A neutral stability value does not show the variant is tolerated. The result does not measure DNA binding or dimerisation. The ClinVar gain-of-function note conflicts with UniProt's loss-of-function annotation and this test does not resolve that.

payload.why: T1 measured +1.96 kcal/mol, below the 2.0 threshold at pLDDT 88.0 [T1], which weakens the folding hypothesis H2. The UniProt annotation of reduced DNA-binding for this substitution [E2] then makes H1 the favoured mechanism. The decision is provisional because the stability value is marginal and H1 has not been tested directly.

payload.description: Run the structure comparison (T3) on the 182-581 construct once a structure provider is available and the human approval is granted, and check whether the R382W local geometry changes at the DNA-contacting surface. Confirm H1 if the local rearrangement is small and the residue lies at the domain DNA-binding surface; overturn it if the residue shows no DNA-facing contact. A direct DNA-binding assay (laboratory) would be the decisive test beyond this run.
payload.why_now: T1 weakened H2, so the next test should check the leading mechanism H1 and the unresolved H3 if the structure route opens. T3 is currently infeasible (ESM Atlas timeout), so this is the recorded next step rather than a run.

payload.text:
## Question
What molecular mechanism best explains loss of function of STAT3 p.Arg382Trp (R382W), and which single test should check it? [E1][E2]

## Evidence
ClinVar lists R382W as pathogenic with a disease note calling it gain of function [E1]. UniProt annotates the same change as loss of function with reduced DNA-binding ability [E2]. InterPro places residue 382 in the STAT DNA-binding domain, residues 326-464 [E9]. AlphaMissense scores R382W 0.9966 [E3], ScoreCons conservation at the residue is 0.974 [E4], and EVE classes it pathogenic [E5]. Four experimental structures observe residue 382, and all carry arginine [E6]. A 2021 study found most reported AD-HIES variants are dominant negative, yet only six of 135 in-frame variants had been tested [E12]. Gaps: no direct DNA-binding measurement for R382W [G1], no record of which residues contact DNA [G2], and the gain-of-function label conflicts with UniProt [G3].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
H1 (nucleic-acid binding, rank 1) proposes that R382W removes a DNA-contacting arginine [E2][E9]. H2 (stability, rank 2) proposes that R382W destabilises the DNA-binding domain fold [E4][E5]. H3 (protein interaction, rank 3) proposes dominant-negative dimer formation with wild-type STAT3 [E8][E12].

## Tests considered and the choice
Three candidates were recorded: T1, a FoldX stability test, runnable now with no approval; T2, a structural-context test, which ProtVar already reports as having no interface [T2]; and T3, a structure comparison, which cannot run now and needs approval [T3]. T1 was chosen because it separates H2 from H1 at no compute cost [T1].

## Result
FoldX predicts a folding free-energy change of +1.96 kcal/mol for R382W, below the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold, at residue pLDDT 88.0 [T1]. At the same residue, R382Q is predicted at +2.23 kcal/mol [T1].

## Updated decision
H1 remains the favoured hypothesis, so the decision is unchanged [T1]. H2 is weakened because the predicted change is marginal and R382Q is more destabilising yet also pathogenic [T1][E10]. H3 is unchanged because this test does not measure dimer contact [T1].

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
FoldX on a predicted model carries errors near 1 kcal/mol, so the neutral call is marginal [T1]. No DNA-binding or dimerisation measurement was run, and the direction conflict [G3] is unresolved. The H1 ranking rests on the UniProt annotation [E2].

## Next experiment
Run the structure comparison T3 once a provider is available and approval is granted, to check local geometry at the DNA-facing surface [T3]. A direct DNA-binding assay in the laboratory would decide H1 [G1].
